tech.name: Prompt caching (Claude API, OpenAI API)
tech.released: shipped by both makers well before 2026-11; not a new release
tech.status: generally available; on by default for supported OpenAI models, opt-in with cache_control on the Claude Messages API
tech.one_line: When requests share the same start (a long document first), the API saves its work on that start once and reuses it, so later questions pay about a tenth for it and start answering sooner.

predecessor.name: The same requests without caching: the whole 100-page PDF is re-sent, re-processed and billed at full input price on every question

hook.text: Prompt caching means you stop paying full price for the same 100-page PDF thirty times when you ask your AI thirty questions, but how?

claims.text: Without caching, each request processes the whole prompt again: 'Across ten requests, one write and nine full reads cost 2.15x at that rate, compared with 10x without caching.' So 30 questions about one PDF = 30 full PDF reads without caching, about 4.15 with it (1.25 + 29 x 0.1).

before.text: Here's how. Without caching, it's a student re-reading the whole book per question. Question one: all 100 pages, full price. Question two: all again. By question thirty: paid thirty times.

claims.text: Without caching the whole prefix is processed and billed on every request: '... compared with 10x without caching.'
Compute-efficient: Avoid recalculating a prompt prefix that the model has already processed.

new.text: With prompt caching, question one pays a quarter more, by default, to save its work. Questions two to thirty reuse that work for about a tenth on most models, and usually answer sooner. How? The document goes first, the same every time; only the new question is read fresh.

claims.text: Cache write tokens with a 5-minute TTL are 1.25 times the base input tokens price.
cache writes cost 1.25x the standard, uncached input-token rate for the default 30-minute lifetime (GPT-5.6 and later)
Cache read tokens are 0.1 times the base input tokens price (see the table footnote for per-model exceptions).
Subsequent reads cost 0.1x the ordinary input rate on most of these models and 0.05x on GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6.2 Sol, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-6.1 Terra
You generally see improved time-to-first-token for long documents.

Prompt caching preserves that state for a reusable prefix: the unchanged tokens at the beginning of a prompt. When a later request has the same prefix and finds a matching cache entry, the model can reuse the saved state instead of processing those tokens again. It still needs to process any new input to generate a new response.
Cache hits require 100 percent identical prompt segments, including all text and images up to and including the block marked with cache control.
Put stable developer instructions and shared reference material first.

why.text: OpenAI's math: ten requests cost just over two full reads, not ten. Ours for thirty: about four.

claims.text: Across ten requests, one write and nine full reads cost 2.15x at that rate, compared with 10x without caching.
Our 30 questions, same method: 1 write x 1.25 + 29 reads x 0.1 = 4.15 full PDF reads, against 30 (arithmetic on the rates above).
Cached prefixes automatically expire after a minimum of 5 minutes of inactivity.

takeaway.text: That's how you stop paying full price thirty times. The catch: on Claude, unused saved work can fade after five minutes, by default. Same book: read once, reuse the work.

claims.text: By default, the cache has a 5-minute lifetime. The cache is refreshed for no additional cost each time the cached content is used.

background.text: Prompt caching is enabled by default for supported OpenAI models.
Messages API: Opt in with cache_control, at the top level or on blocks.
If 5 minutes is too short, you can use a 1-hour cache duration at additional cost
OpenAI GPT-5.6 and later: default 30-minute lifetime at 1.25x; 12-hour lifetime at 2.5x the uncached input-token rate.
The minimum cacheable prompt length is 1,024 tokens for GPT-5.6 and later
Cheaper input tokens: Pay the model's reduced cached-input rate for reused tokens, discounted up to 95%.

Books, papers, documentation, podcast transcripts, and other long-form content: Make any knowledge base interactive by embedding the entire document(s) into the prompt, and letting users ask it questions.
